title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 9 of the Longue Marche manuscript (archive p.18). Grothendieck lists 'essentially equivalent' profinite descriptions of a finitely generated extension K of Q. This is the dictionary underlying the birational anabelian programme: reconstructing K from its absolute Galois group, or from its geometric fundamental group with outer Galois action.

1) The étale topos B_K (the classifying topos of Gal(K), a 'pro-galoisian' topos), seen as an object over B_Q via the morphism B_K → B_Q.
2) Its fundamental groupoid Π_K, the profinite groupoid of points of B_K (algebraic closures K̄, or universal coverings), seen as a groupoid over Π_Q.
3) The outer profinite group E_K (Gal(K) up to inner automorphisms), lying over the outer group E_Q = Γ_Q. Γ_Q is only defined up to inner automorphisms, hence 'progroupe'.
4) Rigidified version. One describes pairs (K, K̄) instead of K: an object Q̄ of Π_Q together with a homomorphism of profinite groups E = Gal(K̄/K) → Γ_{Q̄/Q}. Here the image is open and the kernel is the geometric group.
5) Fix Q̄ and Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q). Consider pairs (K, i), where i embeds the constant field k (the algebraic closure of Q in K) into Q̄. These are described by the outer geometric group π_K = π_1(K ⊗_k Q̄), with an outer action of the open subgroup Γ_K = Gal(Q̄/i(k)) ⊂ Γ. This is the extension 1 → π_K → E_K → Γ_K → 1 read as an outer action.
6) (Margin.) Fix only Q̄/Q. Use the profinite groupoid Π_{K⊗_Q Q̄}, or the topos B_{K⊗_Q Q̄}, with Γ_{Q̄/Q} acting on it. K ⊗_Q Q̄ is a product of [k:Q] fields, so it has [k:Q] components. This is why a groupoid (not a group) is needed and why the whole group Γ, rather than Γ_K, acts. Variant 6 is the 'induced' form of variant 5.

Purpose: to set up the various equivalent categories (topoi over B_Q, groupoids over Π_Q, outer extensions of Γ) in which the anabelian functor K ↦ profinite data lives. On the next page Grothendieck checks functoriality for field homomorphisms K → K'.
errors: No mathematical error. 'Essentially equivalent' holds only with the appropriate rigidifications: 1)-3) are equivalent as 2-categorical data, while 4) and 5) involve choices (K̄, or the embedding i). Grothendieck flags this himself on the previous page.
In 5), π_1(K) must mean the geometric fundamental group π_1(K⊗_k Q̄), not the absolute Galois group of K. The notation is loose; the next page writes π_1(K) = Γ_K, which adds to the ambiguity.

ideas.what: Describing a function field K/Q by the morphism of étale (classifying) topoi B_K → B_Q, or by its fundamental groupoid over Π_Q
ideas.modern_name: Galois categories / profinite groupoids; birational anabelian setup in topos language
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1, SGA4); anabelian formulation in Grothendieck 1983-84
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoid), Letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse d'un programme 1984 (anabelian, birational version)

ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois representation ρ: G_k → Out(π_1^geom)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard list of equivalent formulations of the profinite data attached to a function field, as later used in the birational anabelian conjecture (proved by Pop). The topos/groupoid language is characteristic of Grothendieck and already appears in his published letters and the Esquisse. Nothing new is stated.
transcription_corrections: In 4), the inserted word under the struck line is more likely 'fixés' than 'finis'.
In 5), 'π_K = π_1(K)' is read with an equals sign; the image shows something like '∓' that is probably just '='. Mathematically π_1 here is the geometric group.
In 2), 'de ses revêt. universels' appears to read 'de ses revêtements universels'; the transcription is plausible.
